sourcedFrom: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line (UNDATED — Steyr prints a document code rather than a year)
cleanIntro: The M1 is the magazine-fed member of the pair and Steyr's published strip is the same two operations as its single-shot sister: two front action screws out and the barrel group off, then the bolt group out of the tube housing. ⛔ The barrel discipline is where this rifle is won or lost — silk noil or cotton wool, never a steel brush, always chamber-to-muzzle, and the patch comes off AT the muzzle rather than being pulled back through the crown.

steps.title: Rotating safety to Safe, bolt handle up 90°, bolt fully back
steps.action: Move the rotating safety to "Safe". Turn the bolt handle ninety degrees upwards to unlock, and draw the bolt all the way to the rear. ⚠ The M1 feeds from a detachable magazine, so take the magazine out FIRST and then check the chamber — an empty magazine well is not an empty chamber.
steps.aside: Turn bolt handle 90° upwards to unlock the bolt.
steps.cite: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line — 10. Removing the barrel group and bolt group

steps.title: Two front action screws, 5 mm hex — then the barrel group forward and up
steps.action: Undo the two front action screws with a 5 mm hex key. Pull the barrel group forward about 10 mm and lift it out of the tube housing. This is the strip that matters, because Steyr are explicit that taking the bolt out is what lets you clean the barrel properly.
steps.aside:
Pull forward barrel group 10 mm 
(0.39“) and lift it. Remove the 
barrel group from tube housing.
steps.quote:
Unscrew the two front action 
screws with hex key wrench 5 
mm.
steps.cite: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line — 10. Removing the barrel group and bolt group

steps.title: Bolt group out of the tube housing — and stop
steps.action: Pull the bolt group out of the tube housing. ⛔ That is the end of the published strip: Steyr's CAUTION directly under it says further disassembly belongs to a trained firearms technician, and the bolt group itself was permanently lubricated at the factory and does not need opening.
steps.caution:
Further disassembling of the weapon should only be carried out by a 
trained firearms technician.
steps.quote:
Pull out bolt group from tube 
housing.
steps.cite: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line — 10. Removing the barrel group and bolt group

steps.title: ⛔ No steel brushes, ever — silk noil or cotton wool
steps.action: Steyr's cleaning material is silk noil or cotton wool soaked in a special barrel oil or a high-quality gun oil. ⛔ Never a steel brush in this barrel. Copper removers are permitted but only exactly as their maker directs — left in too long they attack the bore they are meant to clean.
steps.caution:
Never use steel brushes to clean the 
barrel.
steps.quote:
The recommended cleaning material is silk noil or cotton wool 
which should be soaked with special barrel oil or high quality gun oil 
for pre-cleaning or final oiling.
steps.cite: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line — 20. Cleaning and maintenance

steps.title: Chamber to muzzle — and the patch comes OFF at the muzzle, never back
steps.action: Every pass runs from the chamber to the muzzle. When the patch emerges at the muzzle you take it OFF the rod; you never pull it back through. Steyr tie this to the muzzle crown by name, and the crown is what the accuracy of a .50 rests on.
steps.caution:
Make sure 
to avoid even the slightest wear or damage to the muzzle crown.
steps.quote: Make sure to always clean the barrel from the chamber to the muzzle.
steps.cite: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line — 20. Cleaning and maintenance

steps.title: Up to 70 rounds: wet patch, bronze brush, patch until clean
steps.action: For a normal session — up to about 70 rounds — the sequence is: rifle horizontal on a rigid board, bolt out, a patch moistened with bore solvent pushed all the way through, then a correctly sized BRONZE brush after the solvent's dwell time, then patches until one comes out clean, then a dry patch to lift the last of the solvent. Steyr's brushing rate is one back-and-forth cycle for every three rounds fired.
steps.aside: Repeat this procedure until the moistened patch remains clean.
steps.quote:
Push a correct size bronze brush a several times through the wet 
bore after the recommended dwell time. Recommendation: for each 
three fired rounds perform one back and forth cycle.
steps.cite: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line — Cleaning of the bore (after firing up to 70 rounds).

steps.title: Past 70 rounds: alternate a COPPER solvent and a CARBON remover
steps.action: Heavy fouling gets a different treatment. Steyr describe both kinds and how to tell them apart at the muzzle — copper shows as a copper-coloured residue, carbon as black between the lands — and the cure is to alternate a copper solvent and a carbon remover until a fresh solvent-moistened patch comes through clean. ⛔ This is not cosmetic: they state that heavy fouling raises pressure inside the barrel, causing hard extraction, loss of accuracy, and potentially making the rifle unsafe to use.
steps.aside: copper residue is blue colored, carbon residue is gray colored
steps.quote:
Heavy fouling deposits increase the pressure inside of the 
barrel, resulting in hard extractions, loss of accuracy and potentially 
making the rifle unsafe to use.
steps.cite: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line — Cleaning of the bore (after firing more than 70 rounds).

steps.title: Chamber first, THEN the bore — and wipe the compensator
steps.action: Clean the chamber with a fitting brush or a cleaning-rod section, and then clean the bore again to carry the chamber's solvent out. Wipe all surplus solvent off the receiver and the compensator; solvent left standing on either is a corrosion site on a rifle that spends most of its life in a case.
steps.aside: Wipe away all surplus solvent from the receiver and compensator.
steps.quote:
Always clean the bore after cleaning the chamber to remove bore 
solvent.
steps.cite: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line — Cleaning of the chamber

steps.title: Oil for storage — and take it OUT before you shoot
steps.action: If it is going away for a while, or living somewhere corrosive, lightly oil the bore and chamber. ⛔ And take the oil out again with a dry clean patch before firing: Steyr are specific that oil left in the bore shifts the point of impact, which on this rifle means a first-round miss at distance.
steps.quote:
Before shooting remove the oil from the bore and chamber with a dry 
and clean patch to avoid a deviation of the point of impact.
steps.cite: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line — Cleaning of the chamber

steps.title: ⛔ White line up, and the action screws to 9 Nm
steps.action: The bolt group carries a white alignment line: it goes in with the line matching the upper edge of the tube housing opening, safety lever pressed down, and slid fully home along that line. Then the barrel back on and the two front action screws tightened to 9 Nm with the 5 mm hex key. ⛔ Steyr say plainly why the torque matters — loose screws will affect accuracy.
steps.quote:
Insert the bolt group in such a 
way that the white line match 
with the upper edge of the tube 
housing opening.
steps.cite: STEYR HS .50 / HS .50-M1 Instructions for Use — 1-BA-6101-2, EU-08 (eng/de), printed in the document code line — 11. Reinserting the bolt group into the tube housing

deepAbsentReason: Steyr answer this in a section of their own, and the answer is no. Section 12 is headed "Disassembling the rifle" and its entire content is one sentence: "Complete disassembly of the rifle by the user usually is not required." Section 13, "Disassembling the bolt group", is the same shape — the bolt group "doesn't need to be disassembled. It has been permanently lubricated by the factory", with occasional inspection by a franchised STEYR ARMS dealer's gunsmith given as sufficient maintenance. ⛔ And the CAUTION under the barrel-and-bolt removal closes it: "Further disassembling of the weapon should only be carried out by a trained firearms technician." So the barrel-group and bolt-group removal in the guided clean above is the whole published strip, and nothing deeper has been invented for it.

cleaning.name: BORE — UP TO 70 ROUNDS
tasks: Rifle horizontal on a rigid board, bolt out
Solvent-moistened patch all the way through, chamber to muzzle
Correct-size BRONZE brush after the dwell time — one cycle per three rounds fired
Patches until one stays clean, then a dry patch
⛔ Never a steel brush; ⛔ never pull a patch back through the muzzle

cleaning.name: BORE — OVER 70 ROUNDS
tasks: Alternate a COPPER solvent and a CARBON remover
Copper residue reads blue on the patch, carbon grey
Until a fresh solvent-moistened patch comes through clean
⚠ Heavy fouling raises barrel pressure — hard extraction, lost accuracy, potentially unsafe

cleaning.name: CHAMBER
tasks: Fitting cleaning brush or a cleaning-rod section
Bore cleaned AFTER the chamber, to carry the solvent out
Surplus solvent wiped off receiver and compensator

cleaning.name: GENERAL
tasks: Metal and synthetic parts may be cleaned ultrasonically without damage
Scope mount kept clean and slightly oiled; permanent lubricants on moving parts
⚠ Use one oil for cleaning and a different one for preservation

reassembly: Bolt group entered with the white line matched to the upper edge of the tube housing opening.
Safety lever pressed down and the bolt group slid completely in along that line.
Barrel replaced in its proper position on the receiver.
⛔ Two front action screws tightened to 9 Nm with a 5 mm hex key.
Bore and chamber wiped dry of storage oil before any ammunition is near the rifle.
fncheck: Reassembled and empty: confirm the bolt group went in on its WHITE LINE and slides fully home, and that the two front action screws are at 9 Nm — loose screws cost accuracy and Steyr say so. Work the bolt and feel it unlock and lock cleanly. ⛔ Take the storage oil back out of the bore and chamber with a dry patch before firing, or the first round will not go where the sights say.
